office: the Office national de l'état civil et de l'identification (ONECI)
note: Biometric Update's 2019 report, republished by the Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative: the new card costs 5,000 FCFA (the first biometric issue in 2009 was free), may be issued from five and becomes compulsory over 16; the 2009 cards had a ten-year validity, kept here for the new card. ONECI's own fee schedule wasn't found; the time isn't stated. ONECI's own home page (read 2026-11-03) prices the RNPP stamp for establishing an identity document at 5,000 F CFA, and its service for persons with a disability applying for the CNI as free (not modelled). The age of five and the ten-year term still rest on the 2019 report, whose page didn't answer on 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative, Côte d'Ivoire: Biometric card validity extended amid ongoing politicization of ID (Biometric Update, 2019)
sources.said: The country’s first batch of biometric ID cards were issued in June 2009 with a 10-year validity. ... But it will be charging 5,000FCFA (US$8.60) per card. The initial issuance in 2009 was free ... the card will become compulsory to everyone over the age of 16 . It can be issued to children as young as 5.
